findings.claim: No harness subprocess has a duration bound, violating the project constraint that subprocess integrations 'bound duration plus captured output'.
findings.evidence: run_logged() executes `"$@" 2>&1 | node "$log_filter" ...` with no `timeout` wrapper anywhere in the script; constraint `no-shell-construction` states 'Subprocess integrations pass arguments separately and bound duration plus captured output'. A hung `claude plugin install` / `codex plugin add` blocks until the CI job-level timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each stage invocation in `timeout <seconds> -- "$@"` (or an equivalent bounded runner) and treat timeout as a distinct failure from stage failure.

findings.claim: Sentinel preservation is only verified once, after uninstall, so the spec scenario requiring install, upgrade, and uninstall to each preserve the sentinel is not individually enforced.
findings.evidence: openspec/changes/harness-install-validation/specs/harness-lifecycle/spec.md: '**THEN** install, upgrade, and uninstall SHALL preserve its bytes'; the script calls `require_sentinel "$codex_sentinel"` only after `codex-uninstall`, `require_sentinel "$claude_sentinel"` only after `claude-uninstall`, and `require_sentinel "$opencode_sentinel"` only after `opencode-uninstall`.
findings.suggested_fix: Call require_sentinel after each mutating stage (install, upgrade, uninstall) for all three harnesses so the failing stage is identified and intermediate clobbering cannot be masked.

findings.claim: The 'upgrade' stages reinstall the byte-identical artifact, so they cannot detect upgrade-transition defects (stale removed files, changed manifests, version migration), despite the design requiring that the lifecycle 'performs an upgrade'.
findings.evidence: openspec design.md: 'performs an upgrade'; but `codex-upgrade` repeats the identical `plugin add compass@compass-plugins --json` against the same unchanged marketplace directory, `claude-upgrade` runs `plugin update` against the same unchanged marketplace, and `opencode-upgrade` runs `npm install --force` of the same `$scratch/$tarball` that was just installed.
findings.suggested_fix: Export a second, deliberately different artifact (e.g., an added/removed skill file or bumped bundle version) and upgrade from the first export to the second, asserting the installed tree matches the new export exactly.

findings.claim: CI no longer compiles or runs any unit test code: the lib/bins test steps and the nextest run were removed, and clippy covers only --lib --bins (not --all-targets), so #[cfg(test)] modules can silently stop compiling.
findings.evidence: Removed hunks: 'Native tests' (`cargo test --workspace --lib --bins --locked`), 'Install pinned nextest runner', and 'Isolated native tests' (`cargo nextest run --workspace --lib --bins --locked`); replacements are `cargo test --workspace --test '*'` (integration targets only, which do not compile #[cfg(test)] code) and `cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins`.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a compile-only check of test code (e.g., `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` or retain the lib/bins test step) so unit test code cannot bitrot undetected.

findings.claim: Parsing the npm pack tarball filename is fragile because the log merges stderr into stdout, so any npm notice containing '[' before the JSON array corrupts the slice and fails with an opaque node exception.
findings.evidence: run_logged pipes `"$@" 2>&1` into the log; the parse does `JSON.parse(input.slice(input.indexOf("[")))`. npm routes `npm notice` output to stderr, so notices land in the same log before/after the JSON array.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture `npm pack --json` stdout to a separate file (or use `npm pack --json 2>stderr.log` and parse only stdout), or extract the JSON with a strict regex anchored to the array.

findings.claim: Harness version extraction via awk first/last field over the whole log is brittle: any extra output line produces a multi-line 'version' and confusing mismatch errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract with a strict anchored regex (e.g., `grep -Eo '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -n1`) or parse a `--json` version output where the harness supports it.

findings.claim: Redaction runs after the 64 KiB truncation, so a secret split at the truncation boundary can leave an unredacted fragment (e.g., 'sk-' plus fewer than 8 characters) in the persisted log.
findings.evidence: Truncation cuts `chunks` at maximumBytes before `rendered.replaceAll(/\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b/g, ...)` runs; the `{8,}` minimum means a truncated token tail shorter than 8 chars survives redaction in the file written by writeFile.
findings.suggested_fix: Redact before enforcing the byte cap (redact the full stream buffer, then truncate the redacted text), or lower the minimum and also redact trailing partial tokens at the cut boundary.
